🇺🇸 Did Trump offer the press secretary job to the wrong Dana White?

Donald Trump made a surprise appearance in the White House briefing room on Monday evening with UFC CEO Dana White. He then stepped aside and let White take questions from reporters.

White told the room he'd "always wanted to do this," then said he has "zero political aspirations." He won't be taking the job. At the end of the briefing, Trump asked him once more whether he'd take it or "just stay with this ridiculous UFC."

The stunt follows a Saturday post on Truth Social in which Trump offered White the role of "Press Secretary of the United States." He called White "a violent Fighter and Warrior" and suggested UFC fighters come along as assistants to "defend us against the Lunatic Left." Only on Sunday, after the story blew up, did Trump say he had been kidding.

There is another Dana White. Dana W. White was the Pentagon's chief spokesperson under Defense Secretary Jim Mattis in Trump's first term, an obvious candidate for the job. According to unconfirmed reports, Trump's then chief of staff Susie Wiles put her name forward, and Trump appears to have mixed her up with his UFC friend and announced him instead. The "joke" explanation only came a day later, once the confusion went public. Wiles was replaced by Stephen Miller on Friday. Dana W. White thanked people for their congratulations but said they had "the wrong Dana White."

The White House has had no press secretary since Katie Zacharia was fired in October, four days after she started. The briefing was arranged so quickly that the presidential seal wasn't on the lectern. It's the latest in a series of erratic moves since the Republicans' heavy losses in last week's midterms.
